title_en: Zhongqing Jiye Development Center v. Pingyuan General Company — dispute over futures trading
ruling_gist_en: A futures trading member that privately leases its trading seat to another in violation of the futures trading regulations shall bear legal liability for the consequences of trading on the leased seat. After assuming liability for breach of contract in advance on behalf of the member in accordance with the trading rules, the exchange is entitled to seek recourse from the defaulting member.
keywords_en: Civil; futures trading dispute; second instance; Supreme People's Court; Sichuan Province; Hainan Province; legal person; Interim Regulations on the Administration of Futures Trading; validity of seat transfer; assumption of liability for breach of contract; right of recourse of the exchange; partial support; seat leasing; futures default; exchange advance payment of liquidated damages; futures trading dispute against Pingyuan Corporation
full_text_en:
中青基业发展中心诉平原总公司期货交易纠纷案

Ruling Summary

A member unit of a futures exchange that, in violation of the futures exchange's articles of association, privately leases its trading seat to another party shall bear legal liability for the trading consequences arising from the leased seat. After the exchange assumes liability for breach of contract in advance in accordance with the trading rules, it is entitled to seek recourse against the defaulting member.

Supreme People's Court Civil Judgment

(2000) Jing Zhong Zi No. 94

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): Zhongqing Jiye Investment Development Center. Domicile: 7th Floor, Huaneng Building, Datong Road, Haikou City, Hainan Province.

Legal Representative: Tang Ronghan, Chairman of the Development Center.

Agent ad litem: Sheng Yang, staff member of the Development Center.

Agent ad litem: Li Di, lawyer of Shengda Law Firm.

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Sichuan Pingyuan Industrial Development Co., Ltd. Domicile: Inside the Government Compound of Xiwai Township, Guanghan City, Sichuan Province.

Legal Representative: Liu Han, Chairman of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Chen Long, lawyer of Sichuan Zhizhonghe Law Firm.

Third Party at First Instance: Sichuan Hezheng Futures Brokerage Co., Ltd. Domicile: 6th Floor, No. 118, Section 1, Renmin South Road, Chengdu City, Sichuan Province.

Legal Representative: Zou Hui, Chairman of the Company.

Third Party at First Instance: Chen Zhengzheng, currently whereabouts unknown.

Appellants Zhongqing Jiye Investment Development Center and Sichuan Pingyuan Industrial Development Co., Ltd., in the case of dispute over futures transaction with the third parties at first instance Sichuan Hezheng Futures Brokerage Co., Ltd. and Chen Zhengzheng, both appealed against the civil judgment (1999) Chuan Er Jing Chu Zi No. 14 of the Sichuan High People's Court, and filed appeals to this Court.

This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law, with trial judge Wu Qingbao serving as presiding judge, and acting trial judges Gong Bangyou and Liu Min participating in the deliberation, and conducted the trial in accordance with the law. Court clerk Kong Ling served as the recorder. The case has now been concluded.

The court of first instance found through trial: Sichuan Pingyuan Industrial Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Pingyuan Company) and Sichuan Hezheng Futures Brokerage Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Hezheng Company) were both member units of Hainan China Commodity Futures Exchange (hereinafter referred to as China Commodity Exchange), with member numbers 165 and 107 respectively, and both companies engaged in futures trading at China Commodity Exchange. On April 5, 1997, Pingyuan Company and Hezheng Company entered into a "Seat Transfer Agreement," stipulating that Pingyuan Company would transfer its seat No. 165 at China Commodity Exchange to Hezheng Company, and Hezheng Company would pay Pingyuan Company a transfer fee of RMB 300,000 before April 10, 1997, and thereafter, all rights and obligations arising from the seat would be assumed by Hezheng Company and shall have nothing to do with Pingyuan Company. On April 7 of the same year, Hezheng Company paid the seat transfer fee of RMB 300,000 to Pingyuan Company. On July 3, 14, and 31 of the same year, Hezheng Company transferred RMB 3.5 million, RMB 9 million, and RMB 250,000 respectively to seat No. 165, and attached "payment instructions" on two occasions stating: Because Pingyuan Company (seat No. 165) has other business relations with our company, it entrusted our company to pay margin on its behalf. On July 25 of the same year, China Commodity Exchange issued a special notice to all member units stating: According to the exchange's regulations, the single-side open interest limit for each member in the delivery month of the natural rubber contract is 200 lots. Positions requiring physical delivery for hedging purposes may be exempt from this limit upon approval by the exchange. Single-side open interest limit means that after the R708 contract enters the delivery month (after the close of market on August 1), each member's long or short positions shall not exceed 200 lots. If a member's positions in the R708 contract requiring physical delivery exceed the above limit, the excess positions must be reported to the exchange's settlement center before the fifth-to-last trading day of the month preceding the delivery month (i.e., before July 25), and the required supporting documents must be provided as required; only upon approval by the exchange may the positions be exempt from the single-side open interest limit, and together with the 200 lots within the single-side open interest limit, may only be used for physical delivery and not for closing out positions. At that time, seat No. 165 held 3,600 lots of R708 contracts, and on July 28, it opened 1,000 new lots, bringing the total holdings to 4,600 lots. The available refundable balance on that day was RMB 1,278,358.96. On July 29, 3,500 lots of R708 contracts were closed out on that seat, and 3,150 new lots were opened, resulting in holdings of 4,250 lots. The available refundable balance on that day was RMB 9,266,973.96. On July 30, the "funds settlement statement" issued by China Commodity Exchange to seat No. 165, in accordance with the "Notice on Implementing Paperless Settlement and Other Matters" (Zhongqi Jiaosuan Zi (1996) No. 8), noted: Your unit's margin is insufficient. Please replenish it before the opening of the next trading day; otherwise, no new positions may be opened on the next trading day, and positions will be forcibly closed to cover the margin deficiency! From August 1 to 13, seat No. 165 closed 917 lots but still held 3,333 lots. On August 18, China Commodity Exchange notified Pingyuan Company: Because your company did not pay sufficient funds to the exchange before the bill exchange date, with 3,333 lots constituting a default, the exchange, in accordance with the exchange's "Delivery System," decided to deduct from your company's account a penalty equal to 20% of the total value of the goods, amounting to RMB 37,196,280 (of which RMB 7,692,280.86 was actually deducted). The remaining shortfall of RMB 29,503,999.14 was required to be paid within 7 days. Because Pingyuan Company did not pay the full penalty within the time limit, China Commodity Exchange, from August 29 to September 5, paid the penalty of RMB 37,196,280 in advance to Pingyuan Company's counterparties, of which RMB 29,503,999.14 was advanced.

On May 25, 1998, China Commodity Exchange sent a "Letter on Urging Payment of Arrears" to Pingyuan Company, stating: In accordance with the handling opinions of the China Securities Regulatory Commission on the R708 incident, our exchange is currently handling the relevant aftermath. Your company has been in arrears to our exchange since September last year, and as of March 21, the amount reached RMB 29,964,693.68. We hope your company will raise funds as soon as possible to pay the outstanding amounts, and within one day after receiving this letter, inform our exchange in writing of your plan and opinion for repayment. On June 19 of the same year, Hezheng Company issued a statement to China Commodity Exchange, stating: Our company makes the following explanation regarding the R708 trading on Pingyuan Company's seat: Chen Zhengzheng opened an account in our company under the name of natural person Jiang Borong. During the R708 trading process, our company, under the entrustment of Chen Zhengzheng, entered into an agency agreement for natural rubber futures contracts with Pingyuan Company. All executed R708 transactions on Pingyuan Company's seat were the trading results of our company's agency client Chen Zhengzheng. According to the China Securities Regulatory Commission's Zhengjian Cha Zi (1998) No. 30 document, the above transactions were actually directly operated by Chen Zhengzheng himself and are unrelated to Pingyuan Company. On June 22 of the same year, Pingyuan Company issued a statement to China Commodity Exchange, stating: In the R708 incident, our company's seat had been leased to Hezheng Company. The R708 contract trading on that seat was actually conducted by Hezheng Company's client Chen Zhengzheng, and the default was also the result of Chen Zhengzheng's trading. According to the China Securities Regulatory Commission's Zheng Cha Zi (1998) No. 30 document, the above transactions were entirely directly operated by Chen Zhengzheng and are unrelated to this company. It was also found that the China Securities Regulatory Commission's Zhengjian Fa (95) No. 163 "Notice on Further Controlling Futures Market Risks and Severely Cracking Down on Market Manipulation" provides:

1. All futures exchanges must strictly control the total market open interest.

2. T+0 settlement is prohibited, meaning that futures exchanges shall not allow member units to use margins refunded after closing out positions on the same day and profits from closing out positions to open new positions on the same trading day. Futures exchanges that still implement T+0 settlement shall change their settlement method within 30 trading days after the issuance of this notice.

The seat transfer between Pingyuan Company and Hezheng Company was not reported to China Commodity Exchange for review and approval in accordance with the relevant provisions of the China Commodity Exchange's "Member Management Regulations." On April 20, 1998, the China Securities Regulatory Commission issued Zhengjian Cha Zi (1998) No. 30 "Decision on Penalties for Violations by Shanghai Hualong Industrial Corporation and Other Units and Individuals in the Trading of R708 Contracts at China Commodity Exchange," finding that natural person Chen Zhengzheng opened an account in Hezheng Company under the name of natural person Jiang Borong and rented Pingyuan Company's seat for operations, investing over RMB 30 million in R708 contract trading, with a maximum open interest of 23,000 tons. The above transactions were actually directly operated by Chen Zhengzheng himself. The above units and individuals, in the trading of R708 contracts, violated relevant regulations and constituted market manipulation. Pingyuan Company's leasing of its seat to others violated relevant regulations. Therefore, it was decided to declare Chen Zhengzheng and others as persons prohibited from entering the futures market; China Commodity Exchange was ordered to expel Pingyuan Company and other units from membership; Hezheng Company was given a warning.

Because China Commodity Exchange's demand for payment of the penalty from Pingyuan Company was unsuccessful, it filed a lawsuit with the Sichuan High People's Court on December 26, 1998, requesting a judgment ordering Pingyuan Company to refund the penalty paid on its behalf. The court added Hezheng Company and Chen Zhengzheng as third parties to participate in the case. Because Chen Zhengzheng's whereabouts were unknown, relevant legal documents were served by public announcement in accordance with the law. The court froze deposits in Pingyuan Company's accounts at the Guanghan Branch of Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (account number 36924501165177) up to the limit of RMB 2 million (actually frozen RMB 76,291.79); and at the Guanghan Branch of Agricultural Bank of China (account number 8010136952) up to the limit of RMB 2 million (actually frozen RMB 1,641.82); and sealed up 13,509.6 square meters of land under the land use right certificate No. 723 issued in 1995.

After trial, the Sichuan High People's Court held that China Commodity Exchange is a membership-based legal entity approved by the China Securities Regulatory Commission, with an "Enterprise Legal Person Business License" issued by the administrative department for industry and commerce, and has the business scope of providing trading venues for futures contracts such as natural rubber. Pingyuan Company is an enterprise legal person with an "Enterprise Legal Person Business License" issued by the administrative department for industry and commerce, and has the business scope of natural rubber. Hezheng Company is a futures brokerage company with an "Enterprise Legal Person Business License" issued by the administrative department for industry and commerce, and has the business scope of domestic commodity futures agency. Both Pingyuan Company and Hezheng Company are members of China Commodity Exchange and have the qualification to engage in futures trading at China Commodity Exchange.

The "Seat Transfer Agreement" signed by the two parties, because it was not reported to China Commodity Exchange for review and approval in accordance with the relevant provisions of the China Commodity Exchange's "Member Management Regulations," constituted a violation of regulations, and the court did not recognize it. According to relevant regulations, in the course of futures trading, the futures exchange shall bear the responsibility of ensuring the performance of futures contracts. If any party fails to fully perform its obligations under the futures contract on time, the exchange shall perform on its behalf, and after such performance, the exchange obtains the right of recourse for the penalty. Therefore, regarding the R708 rubber contract trading conducted by seat No. 165 at China Commodity Exchange, where 3,333 lots were not paid in full before the bill exchange date, constituting a default, the fact that China Commodity Exchange advanced the penalty of RMB 29,503,999.14 to the complying party on behalf of seat No. 165 is clear, the evidence is sufficient, and it is in compliance with the law, and the court recognizes it. However, after China Commodity Exchange issued a special notice on July 25, 1997, to all members restricting the single-side open interest of rubber contracts, on July 28, it allowed seat No. 165 to open 1,000 new lots, and on July 29, when the available refundable balance of seat No. 165 was insufficient, it violated the China Securities Regulatory Commission's regulations on strictly controlling total open interest and "prohibiting T+0 settlement" by allowing it to open 3,150 new lots. This conduct constituted a violation of trading rules, and such violation was a joint act of China Commodity Exchange and seat No. 165. This act was the direct cause of the subsequent default on 3,333 lots by seat No. 165, resulting in the payment of a penalty of RMB 37,196,280 to the complying party. The liability for default should be borne jointly by China Commodity Exchange and Pingyuan Company, with each bearing RMB 18,598,140 of the penalty. The court did not support China Commodity Exchange's claim for Pingyuan Company to pay the full penalty of RMB 37,196,280. However, because China Commodity Exchange had already paid the penalty to the complying party in advance and deducted RMB 7,692,280.86 from the account of seat No. 165, China Commodity Exchange is entitled to recover the shortfall of RMB 10,905,859.14 from Pingyuan Company. Pingyuan Company's long-term delay in paying the penalty advanced by China Commodity Exchange to the complying party has harmed the legitimate rights and interests of China Commodity Exchange, and it shall bear corresponding civil liability. Therefore, Pingyuan Company's defense that the seat had already been transferred and it should not bear liability cannot be sustained. In this dispute, because the China Securities Regulatory Commission determined that the R708 contract trading was "conducted by natural person Chen Zhengzheng, who opened an account with Hezheng Company under the name of natural person Jiang Borong and rented Pingyuan Company's seat for operations, with the transactions actually directly operated by Chen Zhengzheng himself," Hezheng Company and Chen Zhengzheng shall bear joint and several liability for compensation for the liability borne by Pingyuan Company. Hezheng Company's defense that its losses should be borne by China Commodity Exchange also cannot be sustained. In accordance with Articles 84, 106(1), and 130 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, and Articles 130 and 138 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the court rendered the following judgment:

1. The penalty of RMB 37,196,280 for the 3,333 lots of R708 contracts shall be borne by China Commodity Exchange and Pingyuan Company, each paying RMB 18,598,140;

2. For the RMB 18,598,140 borne by Pingyuan Company, after deducting the RMB 7,692,280.80 already deducted by China Commodity Exchange, the remaining shortfall is RMB 10,905,859.14, plus interest calculated from September 6, 1997, to the date of payment under this judgment, at the highest floating loan interest rate for working capital for the corresponding period as published by the People's Bank of China. Pingyuan Company shall pay this amount to China Commodity Exchange within ten days after this judgment takes effect;

3. Hezheng Company and Chen Zhengzheng shall bear joint and several liability for compensation for the above debts of Pingyuan Company. The case acceptance fee is RMB 160,815, and the property preservation fee is RMB 125,520, totaling RMB 286,335. China Commodity Exchange shall bear RMB 143,167.5, Pingyuan Company shall bear RMB 47,722.5, Hezheng Company shall bear RMB 47,722.5, and Chen Zhengzheng shall bear RMB 47,722.5.

China Commodity Exchange, dissatisfied with the above civil judgment of the Sichuan High People's Court, appealed to this Court, stating: On July 25, 1997, China Commodity Exchange issued a special notice to all member units. This was one of the important measures taken by the exchange in accordance with the China Securities Regulatory Commission's regulations on strictly controlling total open interest to control market risks, and it was a trading rule that every member must comply with. If this rule was violated, the exchange had the right to forcibly close the excess positions in R708 contracts under certain conditions and procedures. Before the R708 delivery month, closing or opening positions was a legitimate trading right of members, and the exchange had no right to intervene. From August 1 to August 13, seat No. 165 closed 917 lots but still held 3,333 lots. Before the bill exchange date, Pingyuan Company failed to pay the delivery funds for these 3,333 lots, once again violating the trading rules and delivery system, and should bear liability for default. Violating the prohibition on T+0 settlement is different from trading on margin. The court of first instance's decision that China Commodity Exchange and Pingyuan Company should jointly bear civil liability has no legal basis. China Commodity Exchange requested a judgment ordering Pingyuan Company to pay RMB 29,503,999.14 plus interest, and Hezheng Company and Chen Zhengzheng to bear joint and several liability for compensation.

Pingyuan Company also, dissatisfied with the above civil judgment, appealed to this Court, stating: The transfer of the trading seat between Pingyuan Company and Hezheng Company reflected the true intent of the parties and was actually performed. China Commodity Exchange's subsequent voluntary and unconditional deduction of funds sufficiently proves that it recognized the transfer fact and waived its defense against the validity of the transfer. China Commodity Exchange's pursuit of Pingyuan Company as a defendant for liability for default based on the trading relationship lacks factual basis. The exchange had fault in inadequate supervision during the R708 trading, but was not ordered to bear corresponding liability. China Commodity Exchange violated the regulations prohibiting T+0 settlement and allowed members to trade on margin, causing seat No. 165 to hold positions on margin for a long time, ultimately resulting in huge losses, and should bear liability for the expanded losses caused by its intentional omission. In summary, in the R708 contract trading, the transfer of the trading seat between Pingyuan Company and Hezheng Company had already become a fact, and Pingyuan Company should not bear any liability according to law. The facts found in the original judgment were inaccurate, the nature of the facts was incorrectly determined, and the penalty was unfair. Pingyuan Company requests that the judgment be corrected according to law.

The facts found by this Court are consistent with the facts found by the court of first instance. This Court also finds: Hezheng Company and Chen Zhengzheng did not participate in the second-instance trial, nor did they submit statements. On September 9, 2000, China Commodity Exchange was lawfully renamed as Zhongqing Jiye Investment Development Center (hereinafter referred to as Zhongqing Jiye). On November 16, 2001, the Enterprise Registration Bureau of the State Administration for Industry and Commerce also issued a written certificate to that effect.

This Court holds: The issues in dispute in this case are whether China Commodity Exchange has the right to recover the 20% penalty it advanced, whether the transfer of the trading seat between Pingyuan Company and Hezheng Company is valid, and whether there was margin overdraft in Chen Zhengzheng's use of seat No. 165 for R708 contract trading. The key issue is whether China Commodity Exchange engaged in any illegal conduct and whether such conduct directly caused the loss from the penalty in this case — that is, whether China Commodity Exchange should bear civil liability for the trading losses of Chen Zhengzheng, Hezheng Company, and Pingyuan Company. From the perspective of legal relationship, this case is about recourse for the advanced penalty, not about the liability for conduct in the trading process on seat No. 165 of Pingyuan Company. According to laws, regulations, and relevant trading rules, as long as the fact that China Commodity Exchange advanced the penalty on behalf of Pingyuan Company exists, Pingyuan Company should repay it according to law. The court should only try this fact. As for the allocation of liability among the parties who conducted trades on seat No. 165, that is a different legal relationship from China Commodity Exchange's recourse for the advanced penalty and should not be tried in this case. Therefore, Pingyuan Company's defense cannot be sustained. Moreover, throughout the entire R708 trading process, China Commodity Exchange operated strictly in accordance with the exchange's "Trading Rules," "Delivery System," and relevant regulations, and there were no issues such as "overdraft" or "insufficient refundable funds." China Commodity Exchange also fulfilled its responsibilities and obligations. China Commodity Exchange, in accordance with relevant trading rules, paid the penalty in advance to Pingyuan Company's counterparties, of which it advanced RMB 29,503,999.14. Pingyuan Company should repay this amount.

The court of first instance found that Zhongshang Exchange had violated the China Securities Regulatory Commission's strict control over total open positions by permitting seat 165 to open 1,000 lots on July 28 and 3,150 lots on July 29. The Pingyuan Company's opening and closing transactions from July 28 to July 29 occurred before the delivery month of the R708 contract, and as its margin was sufficient, Zhongshang Exchange had no right to intervene. However, the court of first instance improperly advanced the time at which Zhongshang Exchange could impose limits on a member's unilateral positions to the period before the delivery month. It can be seen from the letters sent by Hezheng Company to Zhongshang Exchange on June 19, 1998, and by Pingyuan Company to Zhongshang Exchange on June 22, 1998, that Pingyuan Company and Hezheng Company were fully aware of the trading situation on July 28 and 29, 1997. Moreover, during the period of more than one year from the occurrence of the incident until Zhongshang Exchange filed the lawsuit, neither party raised any objection to the trading process of the R708 contract on seat 165 or to the fact that Zhongshang Exchange had advanced the liquidated damages. Whether Zhongshang Exchange violated the relevant provisions of the State Council, the CSRC, or the exchange does not have a necessary connection or causal relationship with the outcome that Pingyuan Company accumulated large positions and subsequently defaulted. The direct cause of the R708 contract incident, including Pingyuan Company's margin shortfall and default, was the risk arising from the illegal manipulation of the futures market by multiple companies and individuals, including Pingyuan Company. The fact that Pingyuan Company held large positions on seat 165 into the delivery month was its intentional act and was unrelated to the exchange's trading practices or settlement methods. Therefore, Pingyuan Company must bear full responsibility for the consequences of its actions. The fact that Zhongshang Exchange did not prevent seat 165 from using margin that was released and available on the same day, i.e., permitting T+0 trading, does not mean that seat 165 engaged in overdraft trading on its positions, nor does it have a causal relationship with the parties' losses. Although such conduct violated the provisions of CSRC Document No. 163 [1995], Zhongshang Exchange's liability is administrative in nature and should not be shared jointly with Pingyuan Company for liability for default.

Although Pingyuan Company produced a "Seat Transfer Agreement" signed with Hezheng Company on April 5, 1997, the several "bank transfer vouchers" for Hezheng Company submitted by Zhongshang Exchange, all dated in July 1997, bore the notation "No. 165 Pingyuan Company" and were accompanied by a payment instruction: "As Sichuan Pingyuan Company (seat 165) has other business dealings with our company, it has instructed our company to pay the margin on its behalf." This shows that Pingyuan Company and Hezheng Company did not disclose any "transfer" to Zhongshang Exchange, but rather concealed their private rental of seat 165. The default on the R708 contract in this case occurred precisely during the period of these fund transfers. According to the exchange's trading rules and articles of association, only membership can be transferred; trading seats cannot be transferred. The private rental of a seat does not produce the legal consequences of a transfer, and the party renting the seat must bear the legal liability arising from the trades. In this case, the relationship between Pingyuan Company and Hezheng Company was neither a membership transfer nor a seat transfer; in substance, it was the rental of a seat. Therefore, Pingyuan Company must bear legal liability for the trading consequences of seat 165. Hezheng Company already held seat 107 on Zhongshang Exchange; its purpose in renting seat 165 from Pingyuan Company was to borrow and split positions, thereby expanding its trading positions and manipulating market prices. The CSRC's "Administrative Penalty Decision Regarding the Violations of Shanghai Hualong Industrial Corporation and Others in the Trading of R708 Contracts on Zhongshang Exchange" (CSRC Penalty Decision No. 30 [1998]) has already found and penalized the illegal conduct of seat rental between Pingyuan Company and Hezheng Company. In summary, Pingyuan Company's defense that it had "transferred" seat 165 to Hezheng Company is untenable. Pingyuan Company was fully aware of the trades on seat 165 and must bear full responsibility for the consequences of those trades. Hezheng Company borrowed seat 165 from Pingyuan Company for use by Chen Zhengzheng. Both have been penalized by the above CSRC penalty decision, and both are liable for the losses resulting from the liquidated damages in this case. Therefore, Hezheng Company and Chen Zhengzheng shall bear joint and several liability for compensation. Pingyuan Company's grounds of appeal are untenable and shall be dismissed. Zhongshang Exchange's claim for full recovery of the advanced liquidated damages is established and shall be supported. Given that Zhongshang Exchange has now been restructured as Zhongqing Jiye, its claim shall be succeeded by Zhongqing Jiye. The judgment of the court of first instance, which contained unclear factual findings and improper rulings, shall be corrected. In accordance with Article 44, paragraph 1, of the Interim Regulations on the Administration of Futures Trading, Article 5, paragraph (1), of the Minutes of the Symposium on Trials of Futures Dispute Cases of this Court, and Article 153, paragraph 1, subparagraphs (2) and (3) and Article 158 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, we hereby rule as follows:

1. Set aside the civil judgment (1999) Chuan Er Chu Zi No. 14 of the Sichuan High People's Court.

2. Within 10 days of the effective date of this judgment, Sichuan Pingyuan Industrial Development General Corporation shall repay to Zhongqing Jiye Investment Development Center the sum of RMB 29,503,999.14, plus interest on that amount calculated from September 6, 1997, until the date of payment determined in this judgment, at the bank lending rate.

3. Sichuan Hezheng Futures Brokerage Co., Ltd. and Chen Zhengzheng shall bear joint and several liability for compensation for the above payable amounts. If the above amounts are not paid by the due date, the matter shall be handled in accordance with Article 232 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC.

The acceptance fees for the first instance and second instance trials, each in the amount of RMB 160,815, and the property preservation fee of RMB 125,520, shall all be borne by Sichuan Pingyuan Industrial Development General Corporation.

This judgment is final.

Presiding Judge: Wu Qingbao

Acting Judge: Gong Bangyou

Acting Judge: Liu Min

January 27, 2003

Clerk: Kong Ling

[Introduction to the Presiding Judge]

Senior Judge Wu Qingbao: born in 1964, Bachelor of Laws, appointed as a judge of the Supreme People's Court in 2001.
